title: sparse-page-regrouper-and-soft-return-policy
author: Asha Patel
body: Motivation: On multi-tenant clusters we observed persistent memory fragmentation in the KV cache under skewed tenant access patterns; small scattered pages prevented reclaim and forced frequent spillovers, increasing p99 latency and I/O cost. This PR introduces a Sparse Page Regrouper and a Soft-Return policy that cooperates with the existing eviction pipeline to reduce fragmentation and smooth spill spikes.Implementation summary: Introduces a lightweight page-scoring pass (Sparse Page Regrouper) that runs opportunistically during low-CPU scheduling windows; it groups cold, sparse pages into compact regions by moving KV slots within the slab arena to contiguous pages, reducing interleaving between tenants. The regrouper is tenant-aware and respects tenant quotas; pages eligible for regrouping are selected by a new score combining occupancy density, last-access delta, and tenant pressure. The Soft-Return policy defers immediate spill reclamation: when pages are reclaimed after regrouping they are returned to the free pool with a short soft-delay window during which the runtime prefers allocation from the returned region, avoiding immediate cross-tenant churn. The combination reduces repeated allocate/free thrashing that previously led to micro-spill oscillations.Key changes: 1) runtime/kv/regrouper.rs: new module implementing scoring, lightweight relocation (memcpy-style), and asynchronous completion hooks; relocation is bounded (max bytes per invocation) and cancellable. 2) runtime/kv/allocator.rs: hook points to accept returned regions and a new compact-friendly free-list ordering. 3) runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs: regrouper is scheduled during low tail-latency cycles and cooperates with continuous batching to avoid head-of-line impacts. 4) runtime/kv/metrics.rs: new telemetry for regroup operations, relocated_bytes, regroup_latency_ms, and soft_return_reuse_ratio. 5) docs/perf/kv-memory-tuning.md: notes and recommended parameters for Dedicated and Private deployments.Performance: Local benchmark (mixed tenant skew with 60/30/10 hot/hot-cold/cold) shows 28% reduction in spill I/O bytes and 18% improvement in tail (p99) token latency under sustained load. CPU overhead measured at ~3% aggregate to the runtime when regrouper runs at default pacing; when regrouper pacing is conservative overhead drops to <1%.Safety and correctness: Relocation is implemented with read-copy-update semantics and uses atomic slot swaps; tests added to ensure no double-refs and proper KV tombstone preservation. Relocation aborts if active references are observed or if tenant quotas would be violated.Rollout plan: feature guarded by runtime flag `kv.regrouper.enabled=false` by default. Canary rollout: enable on 5% of Dedicated nodes for 48h, monitor regroup_latency_ms, relocated_bytes, soft_return_reuse_ratio, spill_io_bytes, and p99 latency. If regressions appear, automatically disable and fall back to existing evictor. Related work: follows patterns from ENG-4821 but takes a different approach than the previous slab-coalescer PRs; references SUP-2145 for customer incident context.Testing: unit tests for regrouper logic, integration tests with synthetic tenant mixes, a new benchmark harness (benchmarks/kv_regroup_bench.py) simulating tenant skew; CI includes deterministic relocation fuzzing.Contributor checklist: ensure linear tickets updated, add runtime flag documentation, verify KMS/HSM no-ops unaffected for Private.Notes: this PR is focused on memory fragmentation avoidance rather than eviction strategy changes; it is complementary to the existing prioritized-evictor and spillback rate-limiter.

review_thread: Diego Morales: Please expand on relocation atomicity and what happens if a write races with relocation.||Asha Patel: Relocation uses a two-phase atomic swap with sequence guards; writes take the new slot and a tremor window ensures writer durability — added unit tests that simulate concurrent writes.||Linus Berg: Concern about CPU overhead on multi-socket hosts; can we add headroom pacing parameter?||Asha Patel: Added `kv.regrouper.pacing_ms` and `kv.regrouper.max_bytes_per_cycle` tunables; default pacing is conservative.||Sofia Chen: Approve after addressing minor docs phrasing and adding metric tag for tenant_id.||Asha Patel: Addressed docs and added tenant_id tag to regroup telemetry.||CI: initial e2e bench failed due to flakiness in relocation fuzz test; rerun passed.||Maintainer (merge): Squash-merge after green CI and canary config added to rollout guide.
release_notes: Added a tenant-aware Sparse Page Regrouper and Soft-Return policy to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill I/O; guarded behind runtime flag and recommended for staggered canary rollout; improves spill I/O by ~28% and p99 token latency by ~18% in skewed tenant benchmarks.
